title: The ring with Rama's name
hook: Rama's ring, carried across the ocean, reaches Sita's hand
carry: rama's name carries the devotee across the ocean

segments.voice: Yesterday: Hanuman painted Rama for Sita, and your line was dhyana: see the form you love, detail by detail.

Back in Kishkindha, the monkey armies set off in four directions, search party after search party. Rama gave only one of them a token for Sita: his own ring, engraved with his name. He gave it to Hanuman. Valmiki says Rama could see that the monkey king trusted Hanuman above all, and that Hanuman would be the one to succeed. Everyone else went searching. Hanuman went searching with a ring in his keeping.
screen: `FOUR ARMIES, FOUR DIRECTIONS.` → `ONE RING, ONE SEARCHER.`

segments.voice: Now, under the shimshapa tree, Hanuman brings it out. Look, my lady: this ring, marked with Rama's name. I've brought it so you'll believe me. Sita takes the ring in her hands, and Valmiki says she is as happy as if she had met her husband himself. Her face shines like the moon slipping free of an eclipse. Words can be faked. But this is Rama's own ring, the one she knew on his hand. Think what it has been through: forests, Svayamprabha's dark cave, a hundred yojanas of sea, past Mainaka, past Surasa's mouth, through Simhika, over Lanka's wall and up a tree. And Hindus have never forgotten it. The Hanuman Chalisa, the hymn so many Hindus know by heart, gives it a line: keeping the Lord's ring in his mouth, he leapt the ocean, and no wonder. Why no wonder? Many teachers read it this way: Hanuman didn't cross on strength alone. He carried Rama's name with him. Hindus speak of life itself as an ocean, bhavasagara, the ocean of becoming, and of the Lord's name as what carries a devotee across. That's why people write Shri Ram at the top of a page, say it before a journey, whisper it when they're afraid. The ring that reached Sita is a promise: hold his name, and the sea can be crossed.
screen: `MARKED WITH RAMA'S NAME.` · `A RING THAT CROSSED THE SEA.` · `THE RING IN THE HANUMAN CHALISA.` · then, large: `THE NAME CARRIES YOU ACROSS.`

segments.voice: If you pray, say Shri Ram once, slowly, and picture keeping it somewhere safe, the way Hanuman kept the ring the whole way across. Then say it again on each out-breath, for a minute. If you don't pray, rest your attention on a ring, a bracelet or a small object someone gave you, or one you remember. Feel its weight, think of what it carries for you, and breathe.
The ring. Rama's own ring, marked with his name, carried across the sea by Hanuman, which makes Sita as happy as if she'd met Rama himself.
Your line: Rama's name carries the devotee across the ocean. Tomorrow, what Sita asks next. Day six hundred twenty, done.

shimshapa.meaning: the tree Sita sits beneath in the grove

Svayamprabha.meaning: an ascetic who keeps a hidden city in a cave

Sampati.meaning: an old wingless vulture, Jatayu's brother

Mainaka.meaning: a mountain that rose from the sea to offer Hanuman rest

Surasa.meaning: mother of serpents, sent by the gods to test Hanuman

Hanuman Chalisa.meaning: forty verses praising Hanuman, traditionally credited to Tulsidas

bhavasagara.meaning: the ocean of worldly life, of birth and rebirth
